messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're rolling a tightened egress firewall rule into prod tonight (restricting outbound to privnet-keystore on port 443). I think this will block nodes that rely on the keystore in other regions. Thoughts?

kyle: do we have a canary region? any known consumers in eu-west-1? :thinking_face:

sam: yes, eu-west-1 uses proxy-keystore-2. Quota on that keystore is already near 85% this week.

anya: Reminder: keystore rotates IPs — firewall by FQDN would be better than CIDR. Current rule is strict CIDR allow -> everything else deny, which is brittle.

kyle: logs show a pattern: last night several GPU nodes failed to complete bootstrap with "keystore timeout" after 20s. snippet: ```kubelet: failed to fetch keystore token: dial tcp 10.11.12.13:443: connection refused```

maria: ok pause rollout? Two tradeoffs: delaying keeps the old risk surface; proceeding will likely cause GPU nodes to fail and trigger capacity loss + oncall pagers.

devops-bot: deploy-check: keystore-ephemeral QPS 5200/6000 (85%), region eu-west-1 spike at 78% for token service.

jen: what about a temporary allowlist for the node subnets to the keystore's ENIs until we move to privatelink? low lift and quick rollback.

sam: allowlist helps but we still hit API quota; also suggests adding per-node caching + exponential backoff in bootstrap. I can push a small patch to reduce token churn and stagger node joins.

kyle: also double-check IAM role boundary — the new firewall rule will add a condition 'aws:SourceVpc' in the keystore's assume-role policy. Our autoscaler pods assume the role from a cross-account agent; the condition will block those calls.

anya: that IAM condition is the kicker. If we deploy the firewall without updating role conditions, provisioning will break even with allowlist.

maria: proposed plan: 1) pause the firewall rollout, 2) open temporary allowlist for node subnets -> keystore ENIs, 3) patch node bootstrap to cache token + backoff (sam), 4) update IAM role condition to include autoscaler agent identity, 5) re-run canary in 2 hours. Agree?

jen: +1. I'll run the allowlist change and monitor warm-pool capacity.

sam: I'll open a quick PR for the bootstrap backoff, link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning/pull/867 (WIP).

kyle: I'll prepare the IAM diff and post it here once ready.

maria: assigning oncall: @kyle @jen @sam. Set alert: if warm-pool healthy < 80% for >10m -> page eng-sre.

devops-bot: alert-rule created: warm_pool_health_eu_west1 < 80% for 10m -> pager eng-sre.

maria: thanks — re-scheduling rollout to 03:10 UTC. Updating the runbook and will post the rollback steps here.

jen: FYI I'll also enable additional sampling on keystore latency metrics during the allowlist window so we can see if latency improves with fewer denied connections.

kyle: posted IAM diff: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/ae4d2 — adds SourceVpc exception for autoscaler role and documents cross-account assumption. Please review.

maria: great. After PRs merge we'll coordinate a short canary (5 nodes, 15m) and validate warm-pool and node bootstrap logs. If anything spikes, roll back firewall rule immediately.

sam: noted. I'll queue the bootstrap patch and push a staged image tag for canary nodes.

maria: closing the loop here — thanks team. I'll leave the thread open until canary completes.
